result.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
result.summary: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully? We investigate this question using MedAgentBench by introducing controlled clinical errors into verified agent trajectories. The experiments include 416 faulty trajectories, eight error categories, and six open-weight LLM judges. By comparing each faulty trajectory with its correct counterpart, we measure whether judges genuinely recognize errors rather than simply flagging more actions as unsafe. The findings show that access to clinical evidence significantly improves judge reliability. When shown only the final answer, judges cannot distinguish errors that leave it unchanged, while flagging 56% of correct trajectories. With full trajectory information, the ability to distinguish unsafe actions from correct ones reaches a score of 0.75, and providing actual EHR responses improves discrimination by 0.39. Surprisingly, including the agent's reasoning does not improve overall performance and reduces detection of incorrectly reported clinical values by 0.18, which remain the hardest errors to detect. MedGemma performed worse than the general-purpose model and was the only judge to miss potentially dangerous medication overdoses. We also find that the benchmark's original grader accepts all 38 trajectories with an intentionally skipped laboratory check, while combining LLM judges with a rule-based checker informed by the full EHR record detects 97% of injected faults.

AI.brief_summary: 在 MedAgentBench 中注入受控临床错误（416 条故障轨迹、8 类错误、6 个开源 LLM 评判者），用故障轨迹与其正确版本配对比较，检验 LLM 评判者能否真正识别不安全动作，并考察 EHR 证据、轨迹与推理文本等输入条件的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「配对故障注入＋逐级增加证据」的诊断协议可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正依赖视觉证据、以及验证器对证据的敏感度，但对象是纯文本 EHR 智能体，迁移可行性仍需判断。
